newsitem.title: USA: News Corp's Murdoch seeks fast Sky okay-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: News Corp's Murdoch seeks fast Sky okay-WSJ.

text.p: News Corp's Rupert Murdoch, who needs Congress to change a copyright law so he can proceed with a satellite-television venture, is looking to hasten the measure through Congress as part of a spending bill, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday.

Murdoch, who needs the change to proceed with Sky, his plan to offer 500 channels through 18-inch satellite dishes, would thereby circumvent potentially lengthy reviews by the congressional panels which usually deal with these matters, the newspaper said in its electronic edition.
Murdoch needs permission to beam local television station signals over his planned national service, the paper said.
The Journal said Murdoch already met Senate Appropriations Committee Chairman Ted Stevens and Rep. Bob Livingston.

The paper said Rep. Harold Rogers, chairman of the House appropriations subcommittee which oversees the judiciary and the Federal Communications Commission, was set to meet Murdoch or his representatives on Wednesday, the paper said.
